rules.rule: A legal playbook contains at least 55 pages and exactly one Superstar page.
The Lead Off area contains up to five chosen starting pages. Any page except a Superstar may be placed there.
The rest of the playbook is shuffled at the beginning of the game.
One random page is drawn from the playbook at the beginning of each turn.
Authentic starter packages preserve their original Superstar, page order, duplicate quantities and fixed Lead Off five.
Momentum pages increase a wrestler’s Momentum and may only be played while that wrestler is in control.
Move pages deal damage and may also be played as counters to an opponent’s Move page.
Special pages provide bonuses or abilities described by their visible card text.
Finisher Move pages are powerful Move pages restricted to specific Superstars.
Every playbook has exactly one Superstar page; Superstar pages define Hit Points, abilities and restrictions.
Only the wrestler in control may play Momentum pages.
A wrestler may play at most one Momentum page before attempting a move. Another Momentum page becomes available only after a successful move while control is retained.
rules.source: Original gameplay behaviour, now locked for the mobile preservation build

rules.rule: Ending a turn gives the opponent the opportunity to play and begins their turn draw.
Letting go of a submission causes the hold to connect, retains control and ends the Specials phase.
Total Momentum is the sum of Ability Momentum and Attitude Momentum.
The five Ability Momentum types are Agility, Knowledge, Strength, Strike and Technical.
A move’s method requirements must be paid from the named Ability Momentum pools before flexible cost is paid.
rules.source: Original card scripts and mobile fidelity audit

rules.rule: The original help states that connecting with a Move gains 1 Attitude and being hit loses 1 Attitude, subject to card-specific modifiers.
Move pages can counter an opponent’s Move page when their counter conditions are met.
Autocounter requires ditching seven pages from the hand unless a Superstar or card changes that cost.
A page stating that it cannot be countered prevents Move counters, Special counters and Autocounter.
Counter-only pages cannot be played as ordinary offensive moves.
Move damage reduces Hit Points. Lower Hit Points make a wrestler easier to pin.
A stunned Superstar cannot play moves, counters or Specials unless a page explicitly permits it.
A Superstar on the mat is vulnerable to move types that require that position.
While in submission, submission damage is applied to the targeted body part until the wrestler escapes, counters or the hold is released.
Warnings and disqualification points are tracked separately; applicable match rules perform disqualification checks.
The first pin attempt is free. Each later pin attempt costs Attitude equal to the number of previous pin attempts.
Pin success is influenced by Hit Points and Momentum, with card and Superstar effects able to modify the attempt.
rules.source: Original executable functions and card scripts

rules.rule: A wrestler taps out when submission points on a body part exceed the applicable Hit Point threshold.
Event Specials may each be played only once per match, with no more than three Event Specials total per player.
Each player may have only one Support Special in play at a time.
Only one Referee Special may be in play at a time, and Referee Specials leave play when distracted.
Pages that ‘count as’ another named page share the same combined playbook copy limit; pages with exactly the same name always count as each other.

verification.detail: 65 recovered starter packages; authoritative ID mapping through CardList.gal.
Original starter order preserved; Superstar excluded from hand; remainder shuffled.
One random page drawn at the start of each new turn.
Strict Momentum-to-move action window enforced for player and CPU.
Named Ability Momentum is consumed before flexible momentum.
Seven-page hand ditch implemented; Jeff Hardy uses six; Big Show draw trigger supported.
First attempt free; later attempts spend Attitude equal to previous attempts. Formula modifiers remain under continuing card audit.
Body-part holds exist; exact tap-out threshold and all exceptions require final audit.
Event once-per-name and three-total limits, one Support per player, and one Referee globally are enforced.
Warnings are tracked, but final disqualification thresholds and distracted-referee exceptions still require exact source verification.
